paragraphs: BrightView Holdings, Inc. is a holding company that conducts substantially all of its activity through its direct, wholly-owned operating subsidiary, BrightView Landscapes, LLC ("BrightView Landscapes") and its consolidated subsidiaries. The holding company and BrightView Landscapes are collectively referred to in this Form 10-K (the "Annual Report") as "we," "us," "our," "ourselves," "Company," or "BrightView."

We are the largest provider of commercial landscaping services in the United States, with revenues approximately 4 times those of our next largest commercial landscaping competitor. We provide commercial landscaping services, ranging from landscape maintenance and enhancements to tree care and landscape development. We operate through a differentiated and integrated national service model which systematically delivers services at the local level by combining our network of over 265 branches with a qualified service partner network. Our branch delivery model underpins our position as a single-source end-to-end landscaping solution provider to our diverse customer base at the national, regional and local levels, which we believe represents a significant competitive advantage. We believe our commercial customer base understands the financial and reputational risk associated with inadequate landscape maintenance and considers our services to be essential and non-discretionary.

We operate through two segments: Maintenance Services and Development Services. Our maintenance services are primarily self-performed through our national branch network and are route-based in nature. Our development services are comprised of sophisticated design, coordination and installation of landscapes at some of the most recognizable corporate, athletic and university complexes and showcase highly visible work that is paramount to our customers' perception of our brand as a market leader.

As the number one player in the highly attractive and growing $124 billion commercial landscape maintenance and snow removal market, we believe our size and scale present several compelling value propositions for our customers, and allow us to offer a single-source landscaping services solution to a diverse group of commercial customers across the United States. We serve a broad range of end market verticals, including corporate and commercial properties, Homeowners Associations (HOAs), public parks, hotels and resorts, hospitals and other healthcare facilities, educational institutions, restaurants and retail, and golf courses, among others. We are also the Official Field Consultant for Major League Baseball. Our diverse customer base includes approximately 7,400 office parks and corporate campuses, 6,100 residential communities, and 500 educational institutions. We believe that due to our geographic scale and breadth of service offerings, we are the only commercial landscaping services provider able to service clients whose geographically disperse locations require a broad range of landscaping services delivered consistently and with high quality. Our top ten customers accounted for approximately 17% of our fiscal 2025 revenues, with no single customer accounting for more than 4% of our fiscal 2025 revenues.

Our business model is characterized by stable, recurring revenues, a scalable operating model, strong operating margins, limited capital expenditures and low working capital requirements that together generate significant Adjusted Free Cash Flow. For the year ended September 30, 2025, we generated net service revenues of $2,672.8 million, net income of $56.0 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $352.3 million, with a net income margin of 2.1% and an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 13.2%. For a reconciliation of Adjusted Free Cash Flow, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin to their most directly comparable GAAP measures, see "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" in Item 2. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations.

We deliver our broad range of services through two operating segments: Maintenance Services and Development Services. We serve a geographically diverse set of customers through our strategically located network of branches, as illustrated below.

Our Maintenance Services segment delivers a full suite of recurring commercial landscaping services ranging from mowing, gardening, mulching and snow removal, to more horticulturally advanced services, such as water management, irrigation maintenance, tree care and golf course maintenance. Our maintenance services customers include Fortune 500 corporate campuses and commercial properties, HOAs, public parks, leading international hotels and resorts, airport authorities, municipalities, hospitals and other healthcare facilities, educational institutions, restaurants and retail, and golf courses, among others. In addition to contracted maintenance services, we also have a strong track record of providing value-added landscape enhancements, defined as supplemental, non-contract specified maintenance or improvement services which are typically sold by our account managers to our maintenance services customers. These landscape enhancements typically have a predictable level of demand related to our amount of contracted revenue with a customer.
We have a strong maintenance presence in both evergreen and seasonal markets. Evergreen markets are defined as those which require year-round landscape maintenance.

In our seasonal markets, we are also a leading provider of snow removal services. These snow removal services provide us with a valuable counter-seasonal source of revenues, allowing us to better utilize our crews and certain equipment during the winter months. Our capabilities as a rapid-response, reliable service provider further strengthens our relationships with our customers, all of which have an immediate and critical need for snow removal services. Property managers also enjoy several benefits by using the same service provider for snow removal and landscape maintenance services, including consistency of service, single-source vendor efficiency and volume discount savings. This allows us to actively maintain relationships with key customers in seasonal markets year-round. A portion of our snow removal business is contracted each year under fixed fee servicing arrangements that are subject to guaranteed minimum payments regardless of the season's snowfall.

The performance of our snow removal services business, however, is correlated with the amount of snowfall, the number of snowfall events and the nature of those events in a given season. We benchmark our performance against ten- and thirty-year averages, as annual snowfall amounts modulate around these figures.
(1) Reflects cumulative annual snowfall at locations where BrightView has a presence.

For the year ended September 30, 2025, in Maintenance Services, we generated net service revenues of $1,891.3 million, including $210.8 million from snow removal services, and Segment Adjusted EBITDA of $245.5 million, with a Segment Adjusted EBITDA Margin of 13.0%.

paragraphs: You should carefully consider the following risk factors as well as the other information included in this Form 10-K, including "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and our consolidated financial statements and related notes thereto. Any of the following risks could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, or results of operations. The selected risks described below, however, are not the only risks facing us. Additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or those we currently view to be immaterial may also materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, or results of operations.

Our industry and the markets in which we operate are highly competitive and increased competitive pressures could reduce our share of the markets we serve and adversely affect our business, financial position, results of operations and cash flows.

We operate in markets with relatively few large competitors, but barriers to entry in the landscape services industry are generally low, which has led to highly competitive markets consisting of entities ranging from small or local operators to large regional businesses, as well as potential customers that choose not to outsource their landscape maintenance services. Any of our competitors may foresee the course of market development more accurately than we do, provide superior service, have the ability to deliver similar services at a lower cost, develop stronger relationships with our customers and other consumers in the landscape services industry, adapt more quickly to evolving customer requirements, devote greater resources to the promotion and sale of their services or access financing on more favorable terms than we can obtain. In addition, while regional competitors may be smaller than we are, some of these businesses may have a greater presence than we do in a particular market. As a result of any of these factors, we may not be able to compete successfully with our competitors, which could have an adverse effect on our business, financial position, results of operations and cash flows.

Our customers consider the quality and differentiation of the services we provide, our customer service, and price when deciding whether to use our services. As we have worked to establish ourselves as leading, high-quality providers of landscape maintenance and development services, we compete predominantly on the basis of high levels of service and strong relationships. We may not be able to, or may choose not to, compete with certain competitors on the basis of price and accordingly, some of our customers may switch to lower cost services providers or perform such services themselves. If we are unable to compete effectively with our existing competitors, or new competitors enter the markets in which we operate, or our current customers choose to discontinue landscape maintenance services, our financial position, results of operations and cash flows may be materially and adversely affected.

In addition, our former employees may start landscape services businesses similar to ours and compete directly with us. While our employees customarily sign non-competition agreements, such agreements do not fully protect us against competition from former employees and may not be enforceable depending on applicable law and/or circumstances. The Federal Trade Commission previously approved rules banning non-competition agreements, which were later vacated. Although this rule banning non-competition agreements has been vacated, we cannot predict with certainty whether, if challenged, a court will enforce any particular non-competition agreement or if future rulemaking in this area will occur. Any increased competition from businesses started by former employees may reduce our market share and adversely affect our business, financial position, results of operations and cash flows.

Our success depends on our ability to retain our current customers, renew our existing customer contracts and obtain new business. Our ability to do so generally depends on a variety of factors, including the quality, price and responsiveness of our services, as well as our ability to market these services effectively and differentiate ourselves from our competitors. We largely seek to differentiate ourselves from our competitors on the basis of high levels of service, breadth of service offerings and strong relationships and may not be able to, or may choose not to, compete with certain competitors on the basis of price. There can be no assurance that we will be able to obtain new business, renew existing customer contracts at the same or higher levels of pricing or that our current customers will not elect to self-operate or terminate contracts with us. In our Maintenance Services segment, we primarily provide services pursuant to agreements that are cancelable by either party upon 30-days' notice. Consequently, our customers can unilaterally terminate all services pursuant to the terms of our service agreements, without penalty.

paragraphs: The following discussion contains management's discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations and should be read together with our audited consolidated financial statements and the related notes thereto included elsewhere in this Form 10-K.

This section of this Form 10-K generally discusses the fiscal years ended September 30, 2025 and 2024 and year to year comparisons between the fiscal years ended September 30, 2025 and 2024. The discussion around results of operations for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2023 and a comparison of our results for the fiscal years ended September 30, 2024 and 2023 is included in Item 7, Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for fiscal year ended September 30, 2024, filed with the SEC on November 13, 2024 and is incorporated by reference herein (Fiscal Year Ended September 30, 2024 10-K).

Some of the information contained in this discussion and analysis, including information with respect to our plans and strategy for our business, includes forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. You should review "Item 1A. Risk Factors" and the "Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" sections of this Form 10-K for a discussion of important factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from the results described in or implied by the forward-looking statements contained in the following discussion and analysis.

We are the largest provider of commercial landscaping services in the United States, with revenues approximately 4 times those of our next largest commercial landscaping competitor. We provide commercial landscaping services ranging from landscape maintenance and enhancements to tree care and landscape development. We operate through a differentiated and integrated national service model which systematically delivers services at the local level by combining our network of over 265 branches with a qualified service partner network. Our branch delivery model underpins our position as a single-source end-to-end landscaping solution provider to our diverse customer base at the national, regional and local levels, which we believe represents a significant competitive advantage. We believe our commercial customer base understands the financial and reputational risk associated with inadequate landscape maintenance and considers our services to be essential and non-discretionary.

We report our results of operations through two reportable segments: Maintenance Services and Development Services. We serve a geographically diverse set of customers through our strategically located network of branches in 36 U.S. states and, through our qualified service partner network, we are able to efficiently provide nationwide coverage across the United States.

Our Maintenance Services segment delivers a full suite of recurring commercial landscaping services in both evergreen and seasonal markets, ranging from mowing, gardening, mulching and snow removal, to more horticulturally advanced services, such as water management, irrigation maintenance, tree care and golf course maintenance. In addition to contracted maintenance services, we also have a strong track record of providing value-added landscape enhancements. We primarily self-perform our maintenance services through our national branch network, which are route-based in nature. Our maintenance services customers include Fortune 500 corporate campuses and commercial properties, HOAs, public parks, leading international hotels and resorts, airport authorities, municipalities, hospitals and other healthcare facilities, educational institutions, restaurants and retail, and golf courses, among others.

Through our Development Services segment, we provide landscape architecture and development services for new facilities and significant redesign projects. Specific services include project design and management services, landscape architecture, landscape installation, irrigation installation, tree moving and installation, pool and water features, sports field services and specialty turf maintenance, among others. Our development services are comprised of sophisticated design, coordination and installation of landscapes at some of the most recognizable corporate, athletic and university complexes and showcase highly visible work that is paramount to our customers' perception of our brand as a market leader.

In our Development Services business, we are typically hired by general contractors with whom we maintain strong relationships as a result of our superior technical and project management capabilities. We believe the quality of our work is also well-regarded by our end-customers, some of whom directly request that their general contractors utilize our services when outsourcing their landscape development projects.

Our Maintenance Services revenues are generated primarily through landscape maintenance services and snow removal services. Landscape maintenance services that are primarily viewed as non-discretionary, such as lawn care, mowing, gardening, mulching, leaf removal, irrigation and tree care, are provided under recurring annual contracts, which typically range from one to three years in duration and are generally cancellable by the customer with 30-90 days' notice. Snow removal services are provided on either fixed fee based contracts or per occurrence contracts. Both landscape maintenance services and snow removal services can also include enhancement services that represent supplemental maintenance or improvement services generally provided under contracts of short duration related to specific services. Revenue for landscape maintenance and snow removal services under fixed fee models is recognized over time using an output based method. Additionally, a portion of our recurring fixed fee landscape maintenance and snow removal services are recorded under the series guidance. The right to invoice practical expedient, defined within Note 2 "Summary of Significant Accounting Policies" to our audited consolidated financial statements, is generally applied to revenue related to landscape maintenance and snow removal services performed in relation to per occurrence contracts as well as enhancement services. When use of the practical expedient is not appropriate for these contracts, revenue is recognized using a cost-to-cost input method. Fees for contracted landscape maintenance services are typically billed on an equal monthly basis. Fees for fixed fee snow removal services are typically billed on an equal monthly basis during snow season, while fees for time and material or other activity-based snow removal services are typically billed as the services are performed. Fees for enhancement services are typically billed as the services are performed.

Development Services revenue is primarily recognized over time using the cost-to-cost input method, measured by the percentage of cost incurred to date to the estimated total cost for each contract, which we believe to be the best measure of progress. The full amount of anticipated losses on contracts is recorded as soon as such losses can be estimated. These losses are immaterial to current and historical operations. Changes in job performance, job conditions and estimated profitability, including final contract settlements, may result in revisions to costs and revenue and are recognized in the period in which the revisions are determined.

Cost of services provided is comprised of direct costs we incur associated with our operations during a period and includes employee costs, subcontractor costs, purchased materials, and operating equipment and vehicle costs. Employee costs consist of wages and other labor-related expenses, including benefits, workers compensation and healthcare costs, for those employees involved in delivering our services. Subcontractor costs consist of costs relating to our qualified service partner network in our Maintenance Services segment and subcontractors we engage from time to time in our Development Services segment. When our use of subcontractors increases, we may experience incrementally higher costs of services provided. Operating equipment and vehicle costs primarily consist of depreciation related to branch operating equipment and vehicles and related fuel expenses. A large component of our costs are variable, such as labor, subcontractor expense, fuel and materials.
Selling, General and Administrative Expense

Selling, general and administrative expense consists of costs incurred related to compensation and benefits for management, sales and administrative personnel, equity-based compensation, branch and office rent and facility operating costs, depreciation expense related to branch and office locations, as well as professional fees, software costs, goodwill impairment, and other miscellaneous expenses. Corporate expenses, including corporate executive compensation, finance, legal and information technology, are included in consolidated selling, general and administrative expense.
Gain on divestiture consists of the realized gain on sale and transaction related expenses from the divestiture of U.S. Lawns on January 12, 2024.

paragraphs: BrightView Holdings, Inc. 為一間控股公司，其幾乎所有活動均透過其直接、完全擁有之營運子公司 BrightView Landscapes, LLC ("BrightView Landscapes") 及其合併子公司進行。此 Form 10-K ("年度報告") 中，控股公司與 BrightView Landscapes 合稱為 "we," "us," "our," "ourselves," "Company," 或 "BrightView."

我們是美國最大的商業園藝服務供應商，營收約為第二大商業園藝競爭對手的 4 倍。我們提供商業園藝服務，範圍從園藝維護與改善、樹木照顧到園區開發。我們透過差異化且整合的全國性服務模式運作，透過超過 265 個據點網路與合格服務夥伴網路，系統性地在地方層面提供服務。我們的據點運作模式使我們成為對多樣化客戶羣體在國家、區域及地方層面提供一站式園藝解決方案的供應商，我們認為這代表了顯著的競爭優勢。我們相信，我們的商業客戶瞭解不當園藝維護所帶來的財務與聲譽風險，並認為我們的服務是必要且非選擇性的。
我們透過兩個應報告分部運作：維護服務與開發服務。我們的維護服務主要透過我們的全國據點網路自行執行，屬於路線型服務。我們的開發服務包含為一些最知名企業、體育與大學複合體設計、協調與安裝園區，並展示高度可見的工程，對客戶對我們品牌作為市場領導者的看法至關重要。

作為美國總計 124 十億美元商業園藝維護與除雪市場的首名玩家，我們相信我們的規模與規模帶來多種對客戶有吸引力的價值主張，並使我們能為美國多樣化的商業客戶提供一站式園藝服務解決方案。我們服務的終端市場垂直領域包括企業與商業不動產、住宅社區 (HOAs)、公共公園、飯店與度假村、醫院及其他醫療設施、教育機構、餐廳與零售業，以及高爾夫球場等。我們也是美國職業棒球大聯盟 (Major League Baseball) 的官方場地顧問。我們的多樣化客戶羣包括約 7,400 個辦公園區與企業校區、6,100 個住宅社區，以及 500 個教育機構。我們相信，由於我們的地理規模與服務項目廣度，我們是唯一能為地理上分散的客戶提供廣範園藝服務，且能持續以高品質交付的商業園藝服務供應商。我們前十大客戶在財務 2025 年營收中約佔 17%，其中無任何單一客戶佔比超過財務 2025 年營收的 4%。

我們的業務模式特徵為穩定且反覆的營收、可擴展的運營模式、強勁的運營毛利率、有限的資本支出與低營運資金需求，這些共同產生顯著的調整後自由現金流。截至 2025 年 9 月 30 日財務年度，我們產生淨服務營收 2,672.8 百萬美元、淨利潤 56.0 百萬美元與調整後 EBITDA 352.3 百萬美元，淨利潤毛利率為 2.1%，調整後 EBITDA 毛利率為 13.2%。有關調整後自由現金流、調整後 EBITDA 及調整後 EBITDA 毛利率與其最直接可比的 GAAP 指標的調整說明，請參閱第 2 項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」中的「非 GAAP 財務指標」。
我們透過兩個營運分部提供廣泛的服務：維護服務與開發服務。我們透過戰略位置的據點網路服務地理上多樣化的客戶羣，如下圖所示。
我們的維護服務分部提供完整的商業園藝服務組合，從割草、園藝、鋪木屑與除雪，到更進階的園藝服務，例如水資源管理、灌溉系統維護、樹木照顧與高爾夫球場維護。我們的維護服務客戶包括 Fortune 500 企業校區與商業不動產、住宅社區 (HOAs)、公共公園、國際知名飯店與度假村、機場管理機構、地方政府、醫院及其他醫療設施、教育機構、餐廳與零售業，以及高爾夫球場等。下圖說明我們維護服務營收的多樣性：
(1) 顯示 2025 年財務年度截至 9 月 30 日的資料。
除已簽約之維護服務外，我們亦有強大的紀錄，提供附加價值之景觀改善服務，定義為補充性、非合約指定之維護或改善服務，通常由我們的客戶經理銷售給我們的維護服務客戶。這些景觀改善服務通常與我們與客戶之合約收入有可預測之需求水平。
我們在常青市場與季節性市場均有強大的維護服務據點。常青市場定義為需全年進行景觀維護之市場。

在季節性市場中，我們亦為除雪服務之主要提供者。這些除雪服務為我們提供寶貴的反季節性收入來源，使我們能更有效地運用人力與特定設備於冬季月份。我們作為快速反應、可靠服務提供者之能力，進一步強化與客戶之關係，所有這些客戶均對除雪服務有即時且關鍵之需求。物業管理公司亦因使用相同服務提供者提供除雪與景觀維護服務，而享有諸多好處，包括服務一致性、單一來源供應商效率及採購量折扣節省。此使我們能全年積極維持與關鍵客戶之關係。我們每年部分除雪業務係透過固定費用服務安排簽約，且不論當季降雪量如何，均需支付保證最低金額。
然而，我們之除雪服務業務表現，卻與降雪量、降雪事件數量及事件性質在特定季節之情形相關。我們以十年及三十年平均值為基準，比較我們之表現，因年度降雪量會圍繞這些數值變動。
(1) 顯示 BrightView 有據點之地區之累積年度降雪量。
截至 2025 年 9 月 30 日財年，於維護服務部分，我們產生淨服務收入 1,891.3 百萬美元，包含 210.8 百萬美元來自除雪服務，以及 Segment Adjusted EBITDA 245.5 百萬美元，其 Segment Adjusted EBITDA Margin 為 13.0%。

paragraphs: 以下討論包含管理階層對本公司財務狀況及營運成果的分析，應與本公司經審計之合併財務報表及其相關附註說明一併閱讀，並包含於本Form 10-K之其他部分。

本Form 10-K之此部分一般討論截至2025年9月30日及2024年9月30日之會計年度，並比較2025年9月30日及2024年9月30日之會計年度間之年對年表現。關於截至2023年9月30日之會計年度營運成果之討論，以及比較截至2024年9月30日及2023年9月30日之會計年度之營運結果，請參閱本公司2024會計年度Form 10-K之Item 7，Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations，該文件於2024年11月13日提交至SEC，並 hereby incorporated by reference herein (Fiscal Year Ended September 30, 2024 10-K)。
本討論與分析中包含部分資訊，包括有關本公司業務計畫與策略之資訊，涉及風險與不確定性之預測性陳述。請審閱本Form 10-K之"Item 1A. Risk Factors"及"Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements"部分，以瞭解可能導致實際結果與預測性陳述中所述或暗示之結果有重大差異的重要因素。

本公司為美國最大的商業園藝服務供應商，營業收入約為第二大商業園藝競爭對手之四倍。我們提供商業園藝服務，範圍從園藝維護與改善、樹木照顧到園區開發。我們透過差異化且整合化的全國服務模式運營，透過超過265個分支網路與合格服務夥伴網路系統化地在地方層面提供服務。我們的分支交付模式支撐我們作為單一來源端到端園藝解決方案供應商的定位，服務我們多樣化的客戶羣體於國家、區域及地方層面，我們認為這代表了顯著的競爭優勢。我們相信，我們的商業客戶瞭解不當園藝維護所導致的財務與聲譽風險，並認為我們的服務為必要且非選擇性。
我們透過兩個應報告分部報告營運成果：維護服務與開發服務。我們透過 strategically located 的分支網路服務地理上多樣化的客戶羣體，遍及美國36個州，並透過我們的合格服務夥伴網路，我們能有效提供全美國的覆蓋。

我們的維護服務分部提供一整套重複性商業園藝服務，涵蓋常青與季節性市場，範圍從割草、園藝、鋪設木屑與除雪，到更進階的園藝服務，例如水資源管理、灌溉維護、樹木照顧與高爾夫球場維護。除了合約維護服務外，我們也具備強大的價值增加園藝改善紀錄。我們主要透過我們的全國分支網路執行維護服務，該網路為路線導向。我們的維護服務客戶包括財富500大企業園區與商業不動產、住戶協會、公共公園、國際知名飯店與度假村、機場管理機構、地方政府、醫院及其他醫療設施、教育機構、餐廳與零售、高爾夫球場等。
透過我們的開發服務分部，我們為新設施與重大重新設計專案提供園藝建築與開發服務。具體服務包括專案設計與管理服務、園藝建築、園藝安裝、灌溉安裝、樹木移動與安裝、泳池與水景、運動場服務與特殊草坪維護等。我們的開發服務包含在一些最知名企業、體育與大學複合體中，進行高度專業化的設計、協調與園區安裝，並展示高度可見的工程，對客戶而言，這對我們品牌作為市場領導者的形象至關重要。
在我們的開發服務業務中，我們通常由總承包商聘請，我們因優秀的技術與專案管理能力而與總承包商維持強勁的關係。我們相信我們的工程品質也受到終端客戶的肯定，其中一些客戶直接要求其總承包商在委外其園藝開發專案時使用我們的服務。

本公司之維護服務收入主要來自景觀維護服務及除雪服務。景觀維護服務，如草坪保養、修剪、園藝、覆土、葉子清理、灌溉及樹木保養等，通常被視為非選擇性服務，並透過年度重複合約提供，這些合約通常為一至三年，客戶通常可於事前30至90日通知後取消。除雪服務則透過固定費用合約或按次計費合約提供。景觀維護服務及除雪服務亦可能包含增強服務，這些服務代表補充性維護或改善服務，通常透過與特定服務相關之短期合約提供。在固定費用模式下，景觀維護及除雪服務之收入於服務期間內按輸出法確認。此外，本公司部分重複固定費用之景觀維護及除雪服務亦按系列指引記帳。根據審計合併財務報表之附註2「重要會計政策摘要」所定義之發票權實務便利措施，通常適用於與按次計費合約相關之景觀維護及除雪服務收入，以及增強服務收入。若這些合約不適用此實務便利措施，則收入將按成本至成本輸入法確認。 contracted 景觀維護服務費用通常按月均勻計費。固定費用除雪服務費用通常在雪季期間按月均勻計費，而按時計費或其他活動基準之除雪服務費用則通常在服務執行時計費。增強服務費用通常在服務執行時計費。
開發服務收入主要按成本至成本輸入法於服務期間內確認，以各合約至今所發生成本與預估總成本百分比衡量，本公司認為此為衡量進度之最佳指標。一旦可預估合約之預期虧損，將立即將全部預期虧損記入帳內。這些虧損對本公司目前及歷史營運而言並不重大。工作進度、工作條件及預期利潤率之變動，包括最終合約結算，可能導致成本與收入之修正，並於修正確定之期間認列。

所提供服務之成本包含本公司在會計期間內與營運相關之直接成本，包括員工成本、 subcontractor 成本、購入材料及營運設備與車輛成本。員工成本包含與提供服務之員工相關之薪資及其他勞動相關費用，包括福利、工災保險及醫療費用。 subcontractor 成本包含與本公司維護服務部門之合格服務夥伴網路相關之成本，以及本公司偶爾在開發服務部門所聘請之 subcontractor 成本。當本公司使用 subcontractor 之比例增加時，可能導致所提供服務之成本逐漸提高。營運設備與車輛成本主要包含支應分支營運設備與車輛之折舊費用及相關燃料費用。本公司成本之大部分為變動成本，如勞動成本、 subcontractor 費用、燃料及材料。
銷售、一般及行政費用
銷售、一般及行政費用包含與管理、銷售及行政人員之薪資及福利相關之費用、股票激勵費用、分支及辦公室租金及營運費用、與分支及辦公室相關之折舊費用，以及專業費用、軟體費用、商譽減損及其他雜項費用。公司費用，包括公司高階管理層薪資、財務、法律及資訊科技費用，已包含於合併銷售、一般及行政費用中。
處置收益包含於2024年1月12日處置美國草坪公司所實現之收益及交易相關費用。

headings: 與本公司業務相關之風險
本公司之業務成功取決於本公司維持長期客戶關係之能力。
若客戶減少其委外業務，本公司可能受到不利影響。
本公司可能無法成功執行其業務策略，包括達成成長目標。
未來之併購或其他戰略交易可能對本公司聲譽、業務、財務狀況、營運成果及現金流產生負面影響。
季節性因素影響本公司服務之需求及營運成果與現金流。
本公司之營運受天氣條件及氣候變遷之影響。
本公司之成功取決於本公司高階管理階層及其他關鍵人員。
本公司未來的成功取決於我們吸引、留住並與員工維持良好關係之能力。
若未能妥善驗證員工之就業資格，將可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
本公司使用 subcontractors 進行特定客戶合約之工作，將使本公司面臨責任與財務風險。
本公司資產之重大部分為 goodwill 及其他無形資產，若本公司判定這些資產已減損，其價值可能降低。
與本公司業務運作相關之法律程序所產生之不利判決或和解，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
稅率提高及稅務規則之變更可能對本公司財務結果造成不利影響。
本公司未能遵守資料隱私權規範，可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
本公司可能無法充分保護智慧財產權，這可能損害本公司品牌價值並對本公司業務造成不利影響。
與我們負債相關的風險
我們的重大負債可能產生重要不利後果，並對我們的財務狀況產生不利影響。
我們的浮動利率負債使我們面臨利率風險，這已導致我們的利息支出顯著增加。
我們面臨交易對手違約風險。
我們的貸款協議包含限制條款，限制我們經營業務的靈活性。
我們可能無法產生足夠的現金流量以償還我們的重大債務償還義務，這可能會對我們的業務、財務產生重大不利影響
paragraphs: 您應謹慎考慮下列風險因素，以及本 Form 10-K 所包含的其他資訊，包括『管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析』及我們的合併財務報表及其相關附註。任何下列風險都可能對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運結果造成重大且不利的影響。然而，下列所選取的風險並非我們所面臨的唯一風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉，或目前認為不重要，也可能對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運結果造成重大且不利的影響。
我們所從事的產業與營運市場具有高度競爭性，增加的競爭壓力可能降低我們在所服務市場的市佔率，並對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果與現金流造成不利影響。

我們營運的市場中，大型競爭對手相對較少，但景觀服務產業的進入門檻通常較低，這導致市場競爭激烈，包含從小型或地方性營運者到大型區域性企業，以及選擇不委外其景觀維護服務的潛在客戶。任何競爭對手都可能比我們更準確預測市場發展趨勢，提供更優質的服務，有能力以較低成本提供類似服務，與我們的客戶及其他景觀服務產業消費者建立更強的關係，更快適應客戶需求的變化，投入更多資源於其服務的推廣與銷售，或取得更有利的融資條件。此外，雖然區域性競爭對手可能規模較我們小，但某些企業在特定市場的影響力可能大於我們。因此，因任何這些因素，我們可能無法成功與競爭對手競爭，這可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果與現金流造成不利影響。

我們的客戶在決定是否使用我們的服務時，會考量我們所提供的服務品質與差異化、我們的客戶服務與價格。隨著我們努力建立為領先且高品質的景觀維護與開發服務供應商，我們主要以高水準的服務與強大的客戶關係作為競爭優勢。我們可能無法，或選擇不以價格作為競爭方式，與某些競爭對手競爭，因此部分客戶可能轉而使用成本較低的服務供應商或自行執行這些服務。如果我們無法有效與現有競爭對手競爭，或新競爭對手進入我們營運的市場，或我們的現有客戶選擇停止使用景觀維護服務，我們的財務狀況、營運結果與現金流可能受到重大且不利的影響。

此外，我們的前員工可能成立與我們類似業務的景觀服務公司，直接與我們競爭。雖然我們的員工通常會簽訂非競爭協議，但這些協議無法完全保護我們免於前員工所成立的競爭公司，且是否可執行視適用法律及/或情況而定。美國聯邦貿易委員會曾批准禁止非競爭協議的規則，但後被撤銷。儘管禁止非競爭協議的規則已被撤銷，我們無法確定如果遭挑戰，法院是否會執行任何特定的非競爭協議，或未來是否會有相關規則的制定。任何因前員工所成立公司而增加的競爭，可能降低我們的市佔率，並對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果與現金流造成不利影響。

我們的成功取決於我們能否留住現有客戶、續約現有客戶合約並獲得新業務。我們能否做到這一點，通常取決於多種因素，包括我們服務的品質、價格與反應速度，以及我們能否有效地行銷這些服務並與競爭對手區隔。我們主要以高水準的服務、服務項目廣度與強大的客戶關係來與競爭對手區隔，可能無法，或選擇不以價格作為競爭方式，與某些競爭對手競爭。我們無法保證我們能獲得新業務、續約現有客戶合約並維持相同或更高的價格水準，或我們的現有客戶不會選擇自行營運或終止與我們的合約。在我們的維護服務分部，我們主要根據雙方可於事前30日通知終止的合約提供服務。因此，我們的客戶可根據服務合約的條款，單方面終止所有服務，且不需負擔罰則。
